source.title: Learning Encoding-Decoding Direction Pairs to Unveil Concepts of Influence in Deep Vision Networks
source.authors: Alexandros Doumanoglou; K. Driessens; D. Zarpalas

page_placements.theme: Non-basis directions (SAE, sparse coding, PCA, k-means, NMF) are more monosemantic than neurons or basis dimensions

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper measures the interpretability and monosemanticity of neuron directions in vision models using concept-label and image-embedding metrics, rather than measuring the original claim's specific mixed-input responses.
record.gate_note: The paper compares the natural latent-space basis (neuron directions) with learned concept directions and reports monosemanticity-related results for the natural basis. Background discussion of superposition and sparse autoencoders is not a result about whether neurons are polysemantic. The reported proxies do not identify a particular neuron responding to unrelated inputs.
record.test_reason: This is a methods paper on learning concept encoding-decoding direction pairs (EDDP). The natural neuron basis appears only as one of several baselines (PCA, NMF, Natural) in tables comparing the authors' method. The paper never asks or concludes whether individual neurons respond to unrelated inputs. Its only neuron-level numbers are mean Network Dissection label precision and an average CLIP-distance score. Both are aggregate interpretability proxies used to rank methods, not rates of a neuron mixing unrelated inputs. The paper does not test architecture, training or regularization effects on polysemanticity, and does not vary activation range or scoring. So no version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that their unsupervised EDDP method recovers ground-truth direction pairs in synthetic data. On real CNNs it finds interpretable, largely monosemantic concept directions that usually beat PCA, NMF and the natural neuron basis on interpretability metrics. Interpretability tends to trade off against influence on predictions. They also show uses in explanations and model correction.
record.recipe_differences: Learns unsupervised encoding-decoding direction pairs and evaluates their interpretability against neuron directions; it does not reproduce the original neuron visualizations or measurements.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported neuron-basis interpretability metrics vary across model/dataset settings and across the precision and CLIP-distance measures.

fits_no_version.finding: With Network Dissection labeling, neuron (natural-basis) concept detectors in the last conv layer of five CNNs have lower mean label precision than the learned EDDP directions: 0.47–0.69 vs 0.72–0.89. They also score higher (worse) on CLIP within-cluster distance M: 6.97–7.5 vs about 6.2–7.1.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Learned non-basis directions in CNN latent space are more monosemantic, by label precision and CLIP coherence, than individual neuron directions.

record.problems: The neuron-basis evidence is indirect: concept-label precision and CLIP embedding distance are proxies, not direct demonstrations of a neuron responding to multiple unrelated inputs. The datasets and architectures vary together, limiting causal comparisons across architectures.
record.rows_left_out: Other natural-basis metrics (recall, F1, AP, S1, S2, mIoU, and influence I1) are not included because they do not add direct evidence on semantic mixing beyond the reported precision and CLIP-distance measures.

untested.parts: No individual neuron is shown responding to unrelated inputs. There is no InceptionV1 and no feature visualization.
The cause of polysemanticity is not tested. Superposition is discussed only in the background (A.23).

Architecture, activation function and regularization are not varied to measure their effect on neuron polysemanticity. The architectures differ, but they are confounded with dataset and serve only as settings.
Activation range and explanation scoring are not varied for neurons. The natural-basis threshold is fixed at the top 0.5% quantile.

record.verdict_notes: The reader overstated the relation. The neuron-basis numbers are baselines in a method benchmark, not a test of polysemanticity, and the paper draws no conclusion about neurons being polysemantic. Several rows also carry the wrong cluster-count condition: Natural is reported only at I=D.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test the cited InceptionV1 neuron or directly show individual neurons responding strongly to several unrelated inputs.
Language models and transformer MLP neurons.
Whether polysemanticity is caused by superposition or capacity pressure.
Polysemanticity caused by initialization, regularization, or training noise without capacity pressure.
Does not isolate causal effects of architecture, activation function, or regularization; does not test whether polysemanticity can be lowered without a large performance loss.
Does not investigate whether canonical polysemantic neurons detect a shared feature or related offshoots of one job.
Does not vary activation ranges or explanation methods; its different reported interpretability metrics are proxies for semantic coherence.

relation.reason: The natural basis is only a comparator for interpretability and influence. There is no neuron-level analysis of unrelated co-activation, and polysemantic neurons are never discussed in the main text.

tranche.reason: Methods paper. Neuron directions (Natural basis, at I=D) are one of several baselines for its own EDDP method. It never asks whether neurons respond to unrelated inputs. T4 or T6 both fit; it does not test the claim.

source_check.notes: All 10 values are right, but 8 rows give I=7/8D. The Natural basis is reported only at I=D (512, 1280, 2048, 512, 2048). Neuron precision uses Network Dissection labels at a top-0.5% quantile threshold. M is the mean within-cluster CLIP ViT-B/16 distance over the top 100 images. Both are purity proxies that cannot show unrelated mixtures, so cannot_determine fits.

statements.correction: Last conv layer of ResNet18/Places365, EfficientNet-b0, Inception-v3 and VGG16 (ImageNet), and ResNet50/MiT. Natural-basis mean precision: 0.69, 0.56, 0.58, 0.58, 0.47. EDDP-U/C precision over all I: ResNet18 0.81-0.83, EfficientNet 0.72-0.76, Inception-v3 0.75-0.89, VGG16 0.59-0.63, ResNet50 0.72-0.78 (overall 0.59-0.89). At I=D, VGG16 EDDP 0.61/0.62 vs neurons 0.58. M at I=D, neurons vs EDDP-U/C: 7.02 vs 6.66/6.73; 7.35 vs 6.81/6.88; 7.35 vs 6.95/7.09; 7.5 vs 6.95/7.09; 6.97 vs 6.29/6.61.
statements.problem: The EDDP precision range 0.72-0.89 leaves out VGG16, where EDDP precision is 0.59-0.63 and the paper says EDDP, NMF and the natural basis score similarly. Neuron range 0.47-0.69, last conv layer, Network Dissection labelling and worse neuron CLIP distance are right.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Natural neuron-direction bases in the five tested vision networks
reader_labels.reason: The reported concept-label precision values are 0.47–0.69, consistent with imperfect semantic purity, though these proxies do not directly establish unrelated mixed responses (r1, r3, r5, r7, r9).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Natural neuron-direction bases across the tested architectures and datasets
reader_labels.reason: Precision and CLIP-distance values vary across tested model settings, but architectures are not isolated from dataset or training differences, and the paper does not test reducing polysemanticity without a performance cost (r1–r10).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Concept-label precision versus CLIP embedding-distance scores
reader_labels.reason: The paper reports both a label-based precision metric and a CLIP-distance coherence metric for neuron directions, but does not vary activation ranges or explanation methods (r1–r10).
